choices.pr_choice: The characterization is named StarAlgEquiv.eq_linearIsometryEquivConjStarAlgEquiv, following the name pattern of the two existing counterparts.
choices.visibility_reason: Not stated in the brief. The brief names the two counterparts (they come from the description's first paragraph), whose name pattern makes this name predictable, so a designer match here is weak evidence.
choices.consequence: The name governs discoverability and dot notation on star-algebra equivalences; a name off the counterparts' pattern would break the family a user searches by.

choices.pr_choice: Both the characterization and the order result assume the isomorphism is continuous (forward direction only; continuity of the inverse is derived in the proof), rather than covering every star-algebra equivalence.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief poses (i) every star-algebra isomorphism and (ii) isomorphisms with some continuity hypothesis as two symmetric readings, citing only the title and the existing counterpart's assumption; it does not say which the PR took, the form of the hypothesis, or that it is considered removable.
choices.consequence: Every user must supply continuity of f, and the order instance only fires for maps known to be continuous; the unconditional statement would be strictly stronger and drop the hypothesis from both.

choices.pr_choice: The conclusion is an existential equality of bundled star-algebra equivalences, f equal to the conjugation by U, phrased through the new conjugation definition, rather than a pointwise statement.
choices.excerpt: ∃ U : V ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] W, f = U.conjStarAlgEquiv := by
choices.visibility_reason: The brief states (b) in words (f sends each A to UAU⁻¹). The bundled-equality form is predictable from the existing continuous counterpart, whose statement the designer sees in the base text.
choices.consequence: A bundled equality lets users rewrite the whole map and compose with the conjugation API; a pointwise form would need extensionality at each use and would diverge from the counterparts.

choices.pr_choice: No nontriviality assumption on V or W; the zero-space cases are handled inside the proof.
choices.status_reason: A special case the PR covers (zero spaces), kept as a requirement in section 3 of the brief.
choices.visibility_reason: Section 3 states that (b) covers the case where V or W is the zero space; the protocol makes a special case the PR covers a requirement to keep.

choices.pr_choice: The implementing unitary is a bundled linear isometry equivalence V ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] W.
choices.visibility_reason: The goal cannot be stated without saying what implements f (the title says isometrically inner). The brief uses the standard mathematical notion, a linear bijection preserving inner products, which points toward Mathlib's linear isometry equivalence, though it also fits, for example, a continuous linear equivalence whose adjoint is its inverse.
choices.consequence: Fixes what users must produce or receive; the linear isometry equivalence has broad existing API, an alternative encoding would need conversions.

choices.pr_choice: Conjugation by a linear isometry equivalence is introduced as a new definition returning a bundled star-algebra equivalence between the operator algebras.
choices.excerpt: def conjStarAlgEquiv (e : H ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] K) : (H →L[𝕜] H) ≃⋆ₐ[𝕜] (K →L[𝕜] K) :=
choices.visibility_reason: The kind is decided from the change, which adds this definition; section 1 lists a new definition and 2(a) says the conjugation is available as a star-algebra isomorphism.
choices.consequence: A bundled conjugation is a reusable object (inverse, composition, simp API) and lets (b) be an equality of maps; without it (b) would be stated pointwise and users would rebuild the conjugation.

choices.pr_choice: The conjugation is named conjStarAlgEquiv in the LinearIsometryEquiv namespace, parallel to the existing conjContinuousAlgEquiv on continuous linear equivalences.
choices.consequence: Determines dot notation (U.conjStarAlgEquiv) and discoverability next to the existing conjugation constructions.

choices.pr_choice: The conjugation is built from the existing continuous-algebra conjugation of the underlying continuous linear equivalence via StarAlgEquiv.ofAlgEquiv, so it is definitionally that conjugation and only star-compatibility is proved; continuity is not bundled into the result.
choices.consequence: Definitional agreement with the continuous conjugation lets its lemmas transfer by rfl; a from-scratch structure would need its own proofs and could drift from the continuous version.

choices.pr_choice: The conjugation ships with six API lemmas under these names: pointwise evaluation of it and of its inverse, its composition form, inverse equals conjugation by the inverse, identity, and composition (the last with a third Hilbert space).
choices.excerpt: theorem conjStarAlgEquiv_trans {G : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 G]
choices.consequence: Which lemmas exist and what they are called decides how users compute with the conjugation; missing ones get reproved downstream, extra ones cost maintenance.

choices.where: conjStarAlgEquiv_apply_apply, symm_conjStarAlgEquiv, conjStarAlgEquiv_refl (simp); conjStarAlgEquiv_apply, symm_conjStarAlgEquiv_apply_apply, conjStarAlgEquiv_trans (not simp)
choices.pr_choice: Pointwise evaluation, the inverse rule and the identity rule are simp lemmas; the composition-form lemma, the inverse evaluation and the composition rule are not.
choices.excerpt: @[simp] lemma conjStarAlgEquiv_apply_apply (e : H ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] K) (x : H →L[𝕜] H) (y : K) :
choices.consequence: Sets the simp normal form for conjugated operators (fully evaluated, inverse pushed onto e.symm); another set would change what simp produces in downstream proofs.

choices.pr_choice: The setting is a field-generic RCLike 𝕜 with complete inner product spaces V and W (and H, K for the conjugation).
choices.excerpt: variable {𝕜 V W : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 V] [CompleteSpace V]
choices.status_reason: The title's star-algebra structure on continuous endomorphisms is the adjoint, which the base provides for complete inner product spaces over ℝ or ℂ (section 2 setting).
choices.visibility_reason: Section 2 states the Hilbert-space setting with the adjoint as ⋆; section 4 leaves the field open but notes the base defines the adjoint over both ℝ and ℂ, which points to the field-generic choice.
choices.consequence: Restricting to ℂ would exclude real Hilbert spaces; the setting is the one in which the adjoint star structure exists.

choices.pr_choice: The characterization is between two possibly different spaces V and W, not only for automorphisms of one operator algebra.
choices.status_reason: The description's first paragraph makes it the star version of the continuous result, which is stated between two spaces V and W.
choices.visibility_reason: Section 2 says V and W may differ, sourced to the description's first paragraph.
choices.consequence: An automorphism-only version would not cover isomorphisms between operator algebras of different spaces.

choices.pr_choice: The PR includes the consequence that continuous star-algebra equivalences between the operator algebras are order isomorphisms for the Loewner order.
choices.visibility_reason: The capability section lists what the change provides, so the brief states it as 2(c), sourced to the change alone, and section 4 asks whether it belongs in this contribution.
choices.consequence: Without it users get no order transport along star-isomorphisms of operator algebras; with it the PR also takes on a typeclass instance and its interaction with future order instances.

choices.pr_choice: The order result is a global, unnamed instance of OrderIsoClass at priority 100 for every type F that is EquivLike with NonUnitalAlgEquivClass, StarHomClass and ContinuousMapClass, rather than a lemma about StarAlgEquiv.
choices.excerpt: public instance (priority := 100) {F : Type*} [EquivLike F (V →L[𝕜] V) (W →L[𝕜] W)]
choices.consequence: A class-generic instance enters typeclass search for every equivalence-like type on these algebras and makes order lemmas apply automatically; a lemma would not, and the instance may overlap the general instance the PR's comment expects once a StarOrderedRing structure exists.

choices.consequence: Another file would change which imports a user of the conjugation needs.

choices.consequence: Every importer of the continuous result now pulls in the inner-product-space adjoint and positivity theory; a separate file would keep the continuous result's import footprint small.

choices.pr_choice: The constructor takes continuity of e and of e.symm as two explicit hypotheses, rather than deriving continuity of the inverse.

choices.consequence: Callers must supply continuity of the inverse themselves (the main proof derives it first); a one-hypothesis variant would need completeness assumptions but save that step.

choices.pr_choice: The constructor is named ofAlgEquiv, the same short name as the existing StarAlgEquiv.ofAlgEquiv, which takes a star-compatibility proof instead.
choices.consequence: Parallel names across namespaces aid guessing but mean the two constructors' arguments differ under one name.

choices.pr_choice: The constructor ships with five lemmas: coercion, round trips in both directions, inverse and composition.

choices.consequence: Determines how much of the constructor's behaviour users get for free; fewer lemmas would be reproved downstream.

feasibility_reason: The brief states the task (conjugation by a unitary as a star-isomorphism, the characterization, the order consequence, the Hilbert-space setting, the zero-space case) while withholding the consequential proposed choices: every new name (c1, c7, c22), the statement form of the characterization (c3), the continuity hypothesis (c2, posed as one of two symmetric readings without saying which the PR took or that it is removable), the conjugation's API and simp set (c9, c10), the instance encoding (c14), the public constructor and private helpers (c20, c21, c23-c25), imports (c28) and all documentation (c29-c33). Exposed: the required setting, two-space generality and zero-space case (c4, c11, c12); the implementer described as a unitary in standard mathematical terms (c5), since the title's 'isometrically inner' cannot be stated otherwise; the conjugation as a new definition (c6) and the inclusion of the order result (c13), because the protocol decides kind and capability from the change, with c13's scope flagged open; and placement among existing files (c15-c18) through the packet's base files. The characterization's name and statement form are not exposed but are predictable from the two counterparts the description names, so a designer match on c1 and c3 is weak evidence.
